name: 6-Card Brag
description: 6-Card Brag is a complex partition and vying game that bridges the gap between standard Brag and 9-Card Brag. Every player is dealt six cards and must divide them into two independent three-card hands. These hands are typically played against opponents in sequence (front and back) or used to decide a single highest-rank winner. It rewards both the skill of hand optimization and the traditional bluffing and blind-betting mechanics of the Brag family.

history.origins: Developed as a strategic expansion of British pub Brag, 6-Card Brag introduces the 'partition' mechanic found in Asian games like Chinese Poker but retains the core British vying structure.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Partition variants of Brag appear in Northern English card rooms.
1980s: Standardized as a specialty 'big hand' variant.
Present: Played in competitive Brag circles and high-stakes social games.
history.cultural: Regarded as a 'thinking man's' Brag, where the math of partitioning cards is as vital as the bluffing.
history.evolution: The transition from a single three-card hand to two simultaneous hands forced a total recalibration of betting strategies, as a player might have one unbeatable hand and one complete bluff.

setup.dealing: Ante into pot. Deal six cards face-down to each player. Players divide their six cards into two separate three-card hands.
setup.equipment: Standard pack, betting chips or currency.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the highest-ranked hands across the partition or by forcing others to fold.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Partition**: Players divide 6 cards into Hand A and Hand B. 2. **Vying**: Betting rounds proceed as in standard Brag. 3. **Comparison**: Showdown involves comparing corresponding hands. 4. **Ranks**: Prial > Running Flush > Run > Flush > Pair > High Card.
keyRules: Both three-card hands must be legal Brag combinations.
In many variants, you must win both hand comparisons to take the entire pot; otherwise, it carries over.
Blind betting applies to the entire 6-card set before viewing and partitioning.

strategy.basic: Avoid making one 'Super Hand' and one 'Trash Hand'. A balanced partition (e.g., two Flushes) is often more reliable than a single Prial and a High-Card hand.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Front' Signal: If playing in rounds, winning the first hand comparison puts immense pressure on the opponent. Invest your best cards in Hand A if you intend to bluff Hand B.
strategy.advanced: Range Splitting: Evaluate the total number of trumps and high cards in the 6-card deal. If the deck is 'heavy' with Spades, splitting your Spades across two hands might be a safer defensive move than one strong Flush.
tips: Don't ignore the High Card tie-breakers; kickers are vital in partition games.
If you are dealt four of a kind, you have two pairs or a Prial—choose the split that maximizes your win probability across both comparisons.

variations.name: 9-Card Brag
variations.description: Partitioning nine cards into three hands; the final evolution of the multi-card Brag series.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: No engine overrides; referenced variation shares core Brag structure.

scoring.description: Standard pot-based resolution across dual-hand comparisons.
scoring.winCondition: Win both hand comparisons OR be the last player not to fold.

synthesis.shortDescription: A sophisticated partition variant of Brag. Every player receives six cards and must divide them into two independent three-card hands. Win both hand comparisons to sweep the pot, or use one strong hand to bluff through a weak second. Strategic division is as vital as the bet.
